The microwave ones cover from VHF-UHF to X Band, full polarimetric and very high resolution, along track and cross track interferometry and very high precision multi-baseline capacity for interferometry and tomography applications. The optronic sensors offer very high spatial resolution visible images and fine spectral scene analysis in VNIR and SWIR bands. This paper presents the upgrade and new performances of this flexible platform and the qualification campaign results with various sensor configurations.

articleTitle: An extended target autofocus algorithm for high resolution SAR imaging
abstract: SAR imaging suffers from azimuth phase error caused by platform vibrations and atmosphere disturbances which may significantly degrade the SAR image quality. Traditional phase gradient autofocus(PGA) algorithm can estimate phase error effectively for SAR images with dominant scatterers, and the weighted PGA improves the estimate accuracy by incorporating the variances of different range gates estimates. However, extended targets in high-resolution SAR image will introduce similar distribution for the phase error estimate of adjacent range gates. In this article an autofocus algorithm is proposed to estimate for extended targets situation. First, an method to estimate covariance matrix is presented. Then, a new fusion strategy based on the covariance matrix is investigated to suppress the estimate error. Simulations and real data experiments show the algorithm proposed in this paper has better autofocus results for extended target than traditional PGA algorithms.

articleTitle: Constrained least squares, SDP, and QCQP perspectives on joint biconvex radar receiver and waveform design
abstract: Joint radar receive filter and waveform design is non-convex, but is individually convex for a fixed receiver filter while optimizing the waveform, and vice versa. Such classes of problems are frequently encountered in optimization, and are referred to biconvex programs. Alternating minimization (AM) is perhaps the most popular, effective, and simplest algorithm that can deal with bi-convexity. In this paper we consider new perspectives on this problem via older, well established problems in the optimization literature. It is shown here specifically that the radar waveform optimization may be cast as constrained least squares, semi-definite programs (SDP), and quadratically constrained quadratic programs (QCQP). The bi-convex constraint introduces sets which vary for each iteration in the alternating minimization. We prove convergence of alternating minimization for biconvex problems with biconvex constraints by showing the equivalence of this to a biconvex problem with constrained Cartesian product convex sets but for convex hulls of small diameter.

articleTitle: Development of a Ballistic Missile Defence capability for the SAMPSON multi-function radar on UK type 45
abstract: This paper provides insight into the development and trials of an experimental Ballistic Missile Defence (BMD) capability for the SAMPSON MFR, in service with the Royal Navy on its Type 45 Destroyer. Consideration is given first to extending the current Local Area Defence mission to address new Anti-Ship Ballistic Missile (ASBM) threats, alongside evolution of Sea Viper's ASTER munition. Then to providing a Forward Deployed Early Warning capability for cueing of other BMD systems (e.g. US Navy Aegis), evolving potentially to support full Launch on Remote (LoR) and Engage on Remote (EoR) capabilities.

articleTitle: Through the clouds: Exploring the potential of infrastructure-as-a-service for radar
abstract: As Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) is used in a variety of applications, we decided to investigate the feasibility of implementing compute-intensive radar processing algorithms on a public IaaS offering, Amazon Web Services's (AWS) Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2). We show that for certain radar applications this approach is more cost effective than individual organisations investing in large and complex computing infrastructure, particularly because small organisation infrastructure is often grossly underutilised. By means of example, we hope to motivate other users to consider a cloud computing approach.

articleTitle: Radar micro-Doppler signal detection and extraction via short-time sparse fractional fourier transform
abstract: In order to effectively improve radar detection ability of target with micromotion in complex environment, the principle framework of short-time sparse time-frequency distribution (ST-TFD) is established combing the advantages of TFD and sparse representation. Based on the radar microDoppler (m-D) signal modeled as a linear frequency modulated (LFM) signal, short-time sparse fractional Fourier transform (ST-SFRFT)-based radar m-D signal detection and extraction method is proposed. It is verified by real marine radar that the proposed method can achieve high-resolution and low complexity TFD of m-D signal in time-sparse domain, and has the advantages of high efficiency, good time-frequency resolution, anti-clutter, et al. It can be expected that the proposed methods can provide a novel solution for radar clutter suppression and maneuvering target detection.

articleTitle: Target DOA estimation using nonuniform sparse array for low frequency radar
abstract: For low frequency radars operating at HF/VHF/UHF bands, normally a long uniform filled array is required to obtain accurate target azimuth DOA estimation and good spatial resolution. To reduce the hardware cost, the uniform filled array can be replaced by a nonuniform sparse array. However when conventional DOA estimation technique is used, the sidelobes of nonuniform sparse array will be very high and misestimation may occur. In this article some other DOA estimation techniques, including the classic MVDR algorithm, MUSIC algorithm, and a newly developed iterative adaptive approach (IAA), are investigated for nonuniform sparse array configurations. Their performances are extensively analysed and compared by both simulated and experimental data. The results prove that IAA can achieve good performance for nonuniform sparse array and is capable of resolving multiple targets with only one signal snapshot.

articleTitle: High precision displacement measurements in presence of multiple scatterers using a photonics-based dual-band radar
abstract: In this work, a dual-band photonics-based radar system is described for precise displacement measures in a multi-target scenario. The radar has been designed for application of monitoring and prevention of possible structural failures of buildings and landslides. The radar system exploits the Stepped Frequency Continuous Wave (SFCW) signal modulation and differential phase measurements are carried out on each range bin to evaluate target displacements. The system effectiveness has been already demonstrated in presence of a single target. Here we present a numerical and experimental evaluation of the displacement estimation accuracy in the case of a multi-target scenario. Our study is focused to understand how the presence of multiple targets impacts on their displacement estimates. Simulation results show a typical accuracy of less than 0.2 mm for distances up to 400 m. These results are confirmed by preliminary experimental outcomes, which take into account different operative conditions in a first measure campaign with multiple targets. Finally, concluding remarks and perspectives draw the agenda for our future investigations.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler classification with boosting in perimeter protection
abstract: In security surveillance at the perimeter of critical infrastructure, such as airports and power plants, approaching objects have to be detected and classified. Especially important is to distinguish between humans, animals and vehicles. In this paper, micro-Doppler data (from movement of internal parts of the target) have been collected with a small radar. From time-velocity diagrams of the data, physical features have been extracted and used in a Boosting classifier to distinguish between the classes"human", "animal" and "man-made object". This type of classifier has received much attention lately, but not in radar micro-Doppler classification. The classification result on the current data reaches 90% correct classification with this classifier. The ability to distinguish between humans and animals is good on this data. This classifier type gives insight into the classifier and the utilized features, and is easy to use. A comparison with a SVM (Support Vector Machine) classifier, which is common for micro-Doppler, has also been performed.

articleTitle: Experimental spectral coexistence investigation for cognitive radar
abstract: Cognitive radar offers the prospect of improved performance, or alternatively, the maintenance of existing performance under more challenging conditions, by better utilising the resources the radar system has available to it. This benefit is derived from the active control of the degrees of freedom available to the radar, based on the history of previous behaviours and the associated performance achieved, knowledge of the mission and environment, and the current perception provided by received signals. Waveform diversity [1] is one of the degrees of freedom open to cognitive radar systems. This paper describes an experimental investigation of the use of restricted bandwidth chirps, notched chirps and notched phase coded waveforms to enable a cognitive radar to coexist with a primary user of the RF spectrum.

articleTitle: Overhead power cable Bragg signatures in Ka and Ku band high-resolution SAR imagery
abstract: This paper presents spotlight SAR imagery and measurements that show specular and Bragg scattering from overhead power cables using two airborne high-resolution radar systems that operate in different frequency bands; the K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> (12-18 GHz) and K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> (26.5-40 GHz) band of frequencies. Previous cable measurements show that Bragg scattering occurs at K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub>-band but did not measure Bragg scattering at 18 GHz whilst the measurements and imagery shown here demonstrate that Bragg lobes are measurable in K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> band as well as in K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> band. This paper also shows the advantage of having 50 mm resolutions in both the down range and cross range as this allows overhead cables to be easily distinguishable from the surrounding clutter. The ability to see a consistent set of Bragg locations along a given line for all cables is shown as well as the capability to estimate the same cable surface period with devices that operate at different frequencies.

articleTitle: An investigation of an alternative coordinate space parameterisation for radar target tracking
abstract: Target tracking in radar uses mature methods that have been around for many years. The Extended Kalman Filter has long been the typical choice of tracking filter in radar systems due to its low computational effort and its simple implementation. With many recent advances in hardware and processing capability on airborne platforms, it is now becoming possible to integrate higher-complexity algorithms into real-time systems. This work presents an alternative method of tracking a single target using a hybrid filtering approach with an alternative state space parametrization. This approach will be compared to an EKF, UKF and a particle filter using simulated data and root mean square error.

articleTitle: Research on GMTI signal processing technology of ViSAR system based on low-rank and sparse matrix separation
abstract: GMTI signal processing technology of ViSAR system is an advanced subject in the field of the microwave remote sensing. It possesses the ability of high resolution and high frame rates to realize moving target surveillance, which has broad application prospects in military and civilian aspects. To overcome the inefficiency and insufficiency problem suffered from the traditional GMTI algorithm and inter-frame difference algorithm, the theory of low-rank and sparse matrix separation is introduced for the GMTI signal processing of ViSAR system in this paper. Through the studies in the paper, a fast and efficient ViSAR moving target extraction method is expected to form, which lays the theoretical and technical foundations for the application of ViSAR-GMTI technology in the civil and military areas.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler signature analysis of low-observable marine target in sparse domain
abstract: Recently, it has been proved that sea clutter is significantly variable and sea surface subjects have their micro-motions influenced by the sea state. The micro-Doppler (m-D) signatures can describe the refined motion characteristics of sea surface target, which provides a new solution for detection and recognition. Accordingly, it needs to find new analysis methods for m-D signals, which should possess high-resolution in time-frequency domain, high efficiency, and anti-clutter ability. In this paper, the sparse properties of m-D signal is analyzed and a novel concept named as sparse time-frequency distribution (STFD) is proposed combing the merits of classical TFD and sparse representation. Finally, the micromotion properties in sparse domain are obtained using real radar data, i.e., X-band intelligent pixel (IPIX) radar data and Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) data collected in South Africa.

articleTitle: Ambiguity function analysis of the Inmarsat I-4 and Iridium signals
abstract: Communication satellites systems, such as Inmarsat-4 and Iridium are potential candidates to be used as illuminators of opportunity (IoOs) for passive radar detection and remote sensing. These satellites provide global (Iridium) or near global coverage with exception of polar area (Inmarsat) and hence could be used on entire surface of the earth in contrast to a more commonly investigated passive radar based on terrestrial IoOs, such as DVB-T, DAB, FM etc. broadcasting transmitters. This paper presents analysis of the ambiguity functions of the communication satellite signals, based on analytical study and computer simulation. The potential range and Doppler resolutions of these waveforms are shown and the waveforms' applicability for targets detection and tracking are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Dual-function radar-communication using GPS gold codes
abstract: A dual-function communication-radar system can make better use of hardware resources of an electronic system and is widely concerned in many real applications. In this paper, we study a dual-function signaling strategy that projects communication states to waveforms with good auto and mutual correlation sidelobes, through using Global Positioning System (GPS) short code generation logic. The communication states are projected onto connection statuses of the sub-registers of the Gold code generation logic. The GPS waveforms ensure low auto and mutual correlation and the rich states contribute to a wide communication bandwidth.

articleTitle: A prior elevation range based tomographic SAR imaging for urban building
abstract: The main principle of synthetic aperture radar tomography (TomoSAR) for urban building is to separate the scatterers in elevation stacked in the same range-azimuth resolution cell then the reconstructed three-dimensional (3-D) image can be obtained. However, the reconstruction results will inevitably introduce undesired outliers and bring challenges in extracting and locating the true scatterers. In this paper, by formulating the reconstruction in elevation into the problem of sparse signal recovery, we show that a prior elevation range based modified gridless sparse recovery methods have excellent capability in outliers suppression. Results on numerical simulation and real data experiment are illustrated to validate advantages of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: “Tile”-based airborne phased array radar systems
abstract: Phased Array Radars using Active Electronically Scanned Arrays (AESAs) are now becoming the norm for airborne radar, spanning such diverse applications as fighter radar for fire control and targeting, airborne early warning, maritime surveillance and overland surveillance. This paper describes the results of a project that achieves a step-change in AESA technology by moving to a "tile" based antenna technology to provide much lighter, cheaper arrays, with the aim of making the benefits of AESA radar much more accessible. The initial application is an affordable multi-facet array achieving 360° azimuth coverage. The features of this antenna system are described in the paper, and measured radiation patterns are presented that agree well with modelled behaviour.

articleTitle: Embedding communication signals into the radar transmit waveform
abstract: A joint radar-communication (JRC) system having both radar sensing and communications capabilities is developed to improve the spectrum utilization efficiency. The common transmit array of the joint system is divided into K fully-overlapping subarrays. The transmit antenna elements within each subarray coherently transmit a waveform, and the waveforms transmitted from each array are orthogonal to each other. When the communication receivers are in the radar sidelobe directions, the communication symbol is embedded in both the magnitude ratio and the phase rotation, and circular M-ary Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) is used. When the communication receivers are in the radar mainlobe direction, the communication symbol is embedded exclusively in the phase rotation between each waveform pair, and M-ary Phase Shift Keying (PSK) is used. Under the assumption of medium pulse repetition frequency (PRF), the data transmission rate of the proposed JRC system is in the range of Mbits/s.

articleTitle: Continuous sea clutter models for the mean backscatter and K-distribution shape
abstract: There are a number of empirical models for the sea clutter mean backscatter and the K distribution shape. However, due to the lack of real data, many of these only span a limited parameter space, either covering low gazing angles (typically less than 10°) or medium grazing angles (greater than 15°). As a result, they cannot be used continuously when modelling radar performance or simulating sea clutter for geometries that span both the low and medium grazing angle regions. This paper presents continuous models at X-band for these two parameters focussing on the grazing angle range 0.1° - 45°. In addition, the models cover both horizontal and vertical polarisations, any wind direction, sea states 2-6 and a wide range of radar resolved areas.

articleTitle: High-resolution direction-of-arrival estimation in beamspace
abstract: A novel method for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation in beamspace is proposed to solve the challenging problem of computational complexity reduction under the sparsity of solution. The essence is to map the data from element-space to beamspace by a beamforming matrix, and then the array covariance matrix is used for sparse representation. In doing so, the sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) technique is applied to enforce sparsity at the true signal locations. Numerical results show that, besides efficient computational complexity reduction, the proposed method also significantly improves the DOA estimation performance.

articleTitle: SMARP passive radar for harbour protection and navigation safety: Trials results
abstract: In this paper the results obtained during the trials of the SMARP (Software-defined Multiband Array Passive Radar) demonstrator are presented. The SMARP is a passive radar based on DVB-T and UMTS transmitters developed at Radar and Surveillance Systems Laboratory. The targets observed during the trials involved different class of vessels. The output of the system have been compared with data acquired with an AIS (Automatic Identification System) receiver in order to evaluate the performance of the demonstrator in operational conditions.

articleTitle: Initial investigations into achievable target detection performance in sea clutter with fully polarimetrie radar
abstract: The use of full (quad) polarisation to improve target detection performance in sea clutter compared to single polarisation radar is explored. For surveillance (search) radar, little information is available in open literature dealing with the detection performance gained using a fully polarimetric radar system. In this paper, receiver operating characteristics (ROC) curves are calculated for the three single polarisation cases as well as the full polarisation case. It is shown that a fully polarimetric radar system gives better detection performance compared to a single channel radar system when using an envelope detector. Use was made of the full polarisation IPIX clutter data set and the RCS of the speedboat target was simulated using asymptotic computational electromganetic techniques.

articleTitle: Efficient on-board quantization for interferometrie and multi-channel SAR systems
abstract: In synthetic aperture radar (SAR) applications, raw data quantization represents an aspect of primary importance, since the number of bits employed for radar signal digitization on the one hand defines the on-board memory consumption and the data volume to be transmitted to the ground, while on the other hand it affects the quality of SAR images. In this paper, we discuss a novel approach for efficient raw data quantization for interferometric and multichannel SAR systems, which aims at optimizing the resource allocation strategy as a function of the specific interferometric acquisition requirements. Once the required performance is set (in terms e.g. of phase error or coherence loss), the resulting bitrate is defined according to the expected performance degradation. This is estimated with the help of a priori information, such as high-resolution backscatter statistics as well as coherence maps, which are available e.g. from the latest global data set provided by TanDEM-X (X-band) or Sentinel-1 (C-band). Finally, the desired non-integer compression rate is achieved by dynamically toggling the integer quantization rate of a standard block adaptive quantizer (BAQ). Hence, higher flexibility in terms of performance design and resource allocation can be achieved, without increasing the complexity and the computational load of the quantization scheme.

articleTitle: Sidelobe suppression for random stepped frequency signal based on interpolation and extrapolation
abstract: For random stepped frequency radar (RSF) signal, the sidelobe level of high resolution range profile will fluctuate randomly due to the effects of discontinuous frequency spectra and frequencies hopping. The discrete Fourier transform (DFT) of interpolation and extrapolation (IE) is developed by the Bayesian criteria and minimizing the cost function, which is realized by iterative process. After the IE process, the phase of loss frequencies are extrapolated and recovered, and then the sidelobe of high range resolution profile (HRRP) is suppressed effectively at the same time. Finally the simulation analysis demonstrates that the developed method has better performance of sidelobe suppression in RSF radar.

articleTitle: Word length optimization for sliding spotlight SAR imaging
abstract: With the development of the high-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) technology, the spaceborne SAR has become a hot research topic. However there is a contradiction between hardware resource occupation and imaging accuracy in hardware implementation. Realizing the algorithm with the fixed-point instead of the floating-point is an effective solution for this problem. In this paper we propose a method in which the fixed-point is used for all FFT operations rather than entire operations of algorithm. We simulate the point target and area target. We evaluate the image quality to obtain the relationship between the word length and SAR imaging assessment indexes. The results show that the 13-bit word length can make a good balance between hardware resource occupation and sliding spotlight SAR imaging accuracy in the case of 16384×8192 imaging granularity and 1m resolution.

articleTitle: Lens-based single antenna 24 GHz Doppler radar for precipitation measurements
abstract: This paper presents a highly integrated IQ radar sensor with a single antenna for the velocity measurement of precipitation particles. The sensor measures one desired velocity component of the particles while masking the other ones. This is essential to calculate the amount of precipitation accurately. The maximum measurement error for the desired velocity component is 2.2 %. This is achieved by forming the radar beam with a patch antenna in combination with a dielectric lens.

articleTitle: Effects of mean speed on broadside SAR imagery signatures for accelerating targets
abstract: This paper examines the effects of the mean target speed on the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery morphology of signatures induced by surface movers that are transitioning from a lower to higher speed during the collection interval. The radar platform moves with a constant velocity on a level flight path for the case of a broadside imaging geometry. Recent studies have revealed that such moving target smears are not constrained to have the simple shapes of mere parabolas but instead can display a rich variety of two-dimensional (2D) shapes, including self-crossing signatures. The current analysis investigates the properties of the theoretical 2D central contours of these smears under the conditions of varying the mean target speed for targets which transition from lower to higher speed. It is shown that these theoretical predictions of the signature contour morphology yield excellent agreement with the results of SAR image formation applied to simulated radar data.

articleTitle: SAR Doppler center frequency parameters estimation parallel optimization based on multi-core ARM NEON technology
abstract: Obtaining Doppler center frequency parameters estimation (DCFPE) with low time consumption is a great challenge in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging system. In order to get DCFPE in real time, this paper adopts three parallel acceleration implementation methods-SIMD parallelism, multi-issue parallelism and multi-core parallelism-according to the characteristics of DCFPE algorithm. To verify the efficiency of the proposed methods, the paper builds the ARM embedded Linux system on multi-core ARM Cortex-A9 platform and uses assembly programming language to implement DCFPE algorithm in a 16384*16384 64-bit SAR imaging process. The experiment shows that DCFPE can be accelerated by more than 50% on average with an acceptable accuracy of the result.

articleTitle: The TanDEM-X mission: Global performance of the digital elevation model and beyond
abstract: The primary objective of the TanDEM-X mission is the generation of a global, consistent, and high-resolution digital elevation model (DEM) with unprecedented global accuracy. The goal is achieved by exploiting the interferometric capabilities of the two twin SAR satellites TerraSAR-X and TanDEM-X, which fly in a close orbit formation, acting as Xband single-pass interferometer. Between December 2010 and early 2015 all land surfaces have been acquired at least twice, difficult terrain up to seven or eight times. The acquisition strategy, data processing, and DEM calibration and mosaicking have been systematically monitored and optimized throughout the entire mission duration, in order to fulfill the mission specification. This paper reports the final performance of the TanDEM-X global DEM, which was finalized in September 2016. Moreover, the potentials of the unique bistatic dataset, provided by TanDEM-X, for land classification purposes are discussed. The results confirm the outstanding accuracy of the delivered product, to be exploited by a wide range of scientific and commercial applications.

articleTitle: Simulink based model of a non-planar Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA)
abstract: Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radar systems can steer the array beam pattern from one angle to another instantaneously. In this paper, a generic Simulink based model is proposed to simulate any AESA geometry. This includes the modelling of various building blocks, namely, Transmit Receive Module (TRM), a single antenna element and a combining network. The outputs of the model are the array sum, azimuth difference and elevation difference beam patterns. The proposed model is flexible in a sense that full control of the phase shifters and attenuators in the TRMs is possible to perform various functions. The output of the model is verified against CST simulation tool.

articleTitle: Statistical modeling of SAR images with the generalized Beta distribution of the first kind
abstract: In this paper, a highly flexible model, called the generalized Beta of the first kind (GB1), is proposed to model synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. Many distributions commonly used to model SAR images are special or limiting cases of the GB1 distribution, including the Gamma, Log-normal, Weibull and the Generalized Gamma distributions. A diagram based on the log-cumulants of the third and fourth orders is proposed to represent and classify these distributions, which could provide an easier-to-visualize characterization of a certain distribution in SAR images. Goodness-of-fit test results using measured SAR data show that the GB1 distribution is a more efficient model to characterize the diversity of scenes in SAR images.

Author Keywords: Generalized Beta of the first kind (GB1)

articleTitle: Intuitive quantization of local observations for distributed radar target detection
abstract: Distributed radar has multiple widely separated radar sites connected to a fusion centre with communication links. Signal fusion based detection may achieve the optimal detection performance but needs a huge bandwidth. In this paper, we study a quantization based detection strategy that would first quantize local observations before transmitted to a fusion centre for detection. The quantization rule are designed according to a prescribed fusion rule, under constrain that all events assigned H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> after quantization should have the same likelihood ratio. The method has a low computation cost and low performance loss, as verified by numerical results.

articleTitle: Metamaterial advances for radar and communications
abstract: Metamaterial antennas have progressed considerably in the last few years. Kymeta expects to have its Ku-band metamaterial antenna commercially available in 2017. It is intended for use on vessels anywhere in the world for high speed internet using satellites. Echodyne and PARC, a Xerox Co., have developed a metamaterial array for radar and cell phone usage. The Army Research Laboratory in Adelphi MD has funded the development of a metamaterial 250-505 MHZ antenna with a λ/20 thickness. Complementing this a conventional tightly coupled dipole antenna (TCDA) has been developed which provides a 20:1 bandwidth with a λ/40 thickness. Target cloaking has been demonstrated at microwaves using metamaterials. With cloaking the electromagnetic wave signal transmitted by a radar goes around the target making it invisible. It has also been demonstrated at L-band with a 50% bandwidth using fractals. Stealthing by absorption using a thin flexible and stretchable metamaterials sheet has been demonstrated to give 6 dB absorption over the band from 8-10 GHz, larger absorption over a narrower band. Using fractals material <; 1 mm thick simulation gave a 10 dB reduction in backscatter from 2 to 20 GHz, ~20 dB reduction from 9 to 15 GHz. Good results were obtained for large incidence angles and both polarizations. Using metamaterial one can focus 6X beyond diffraction limit at 0.38 μm (Moore's Law marches on); 40X diffraction limit, λ/80, at 375 MHz. Has been used in cell phones to provide antennas 5X smaller (1/10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> λ) having 700 MHz-2.7 GHz bandwidth. Provided isolation between antennas having 2.5 cm separation equivalent to 1m separation. Used for phased array wide angle impedance matching (WAIM). It has been found that n-doped graphene has a negative index of refraction.

articleTitle: A modified ISAR autofocus algorithm based on single eignvector
abstract: Phase autofocus is a key step of translational motion compensation (TMC) in inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR). In this paper, a modified phase autofocus algorithm is proposed for ISAR to improve the computational efficiency of single eigenvector based autofocusing method. Under the circumstance that a relatively prominent scatterer exists, it is found that the signal subspace can be obtained as an estimation of the phase error caused by target translational motion. In the proposed method, samplings in multiple pulses are used to construct the covariance matrix and obtain the signal subspace, which is equivalent to the existing method with samplings along multiple range bins. Finally, the results of real measured data are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Micro Doppler signature of pedestrian walking on spot at low-terahertz frequencies
abstract: Micro Doppler signature (μDS ) produced by the movements of different segments of human body when pedestrian is walking is often adopted for human detection and identification. μDSs of pedestrian walking on spot at 292 GHz were investigated in this paper to take advantages of the sensitivity of low-TeraHertz (low-THz) waves for enhanced performance of μDS -based identification due to expected high sensitivity of such waves to roughness and texture of target. μDSs from different segments of human body have been recorded and simulated. For comparison, the recorded μDSs at 24 GHz are also shown in this paper.

articleTitle: Suppression of co-channel interference in high duty ratio pulsed radar receivers
abstract: This paper describes a technique for the suppression of interference, particularly co-channel components arising from interference on neighbouring channels, within a pulsed radar receiver operating on a high duty ratio. The technique employs two RF switches with a band pass filter between them and nesting the gating control of the second switch to lie within the gating control of the first switch. Simulations indicate that rejection of in-band interference components arising from interference that is offset by 60MHz from the channel centre frequency some 20dB greater than that of a conventional filtering is possible. The technique is most effective at high duty ratios.

articleTitle: Optimal waveform-based sequential multi-target hypothesis testing for radar detection under unknown clutter parameters
abstract: An algorithm for optimal waveform-based sequential hypothesis testing is proposed in this study for cognitive radar to solve multi-target classification problems with unknown clutter parameters. A closed-loop radar system is designed by estimating the unknown clutter parameters and updating the probabilities of target hypothesis. The prior information is then used to design a waveform for the next illumination based on optimal waveform design method. Waveform sequences are designed and transmitted until one of the total target response hypotheses can be decided by sequential probability ratio testing. The main contribution of this study is that the optimal waveform is designed under unknown clutter parameters and is combined with sequential hypothesis testing. With this method, a final decision can be made using few observations. Simulations show that the proposed optimal waveform-based sequential hypothesis-testing algorithm can significantly reduce the illumination number, and better performance can be achieved both on signal-to-clutter plus noise ratio and on detection rate. Finally, conclusions are drawn based on our analysis and simulations.

articleTitle: Polarization optimization for mainlobe interference suppression
abstract: Controlling the polarization information in transmitted waveforms provides better performance for mainlobe interference suppression applications. In this work, we propose a colocated polarimetric multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar system in where the polarization diversity is employed in the transmit array and 2-D vector sensors are adopted in the receive array. Through analyzing the output signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), the transmitter polarizations can be optimized to obtain the best interference suppression performance. In addition, the target scattering matrix estimation method is studied in this paper. Simulation results demonstrate that interference can be effectively suppressed with the radar configuration, and better interference suppression performance is achieved with the optimal transmitter polarizations.

articleTitle: Fast performance evaluation of detectors with subset simulation
abstract: The performances of detectors used in the fields of Radar and Electronic Warfare, are related to the false alarm probability (FAP) under the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> hypothesis where no useful signal is present in the received data. However, in many cases the probability density function of the detector's output is unknown or very difficult to evaluate. Threshold setting with Monte-Carlo simulations can rapidly become very costly, notably if the detector expression is computationally demanding. In this paper we show how subset simulation procedures recently encountered in system reliability analysis for estimating small failure probabilities can be advantageously used for fast performance evaluation of various detectors applied to high dimensional data.

articleTitle: Operation in littoral environments - The ARTIST multi-function radar demonstrator programme
abstract: This paper provides insight into the experimental development and trials of a potential BMD capability for the SAMPSON MFR, in service with the Royal Navy on its Type 45 Destroyer.

articleTitle: Narrowband radar imaging using NetRAD and NeXtRAD data
abstract: Multistatic measurements of targets and clutter have been performed over the past few years by the NetRAD system developed at the University College London and the University of Cape Town. NetRAD is a three-node, coherent, multistatic, pulse Doppler radar operating at S Band (2400 MHz). NeXtRAD is a new version of this system, operating polarimetrically at L and X Bands. The results obtained by NetRAD have been used for a number of investigations (mostly multistatic sea clutter). This paper reports on results using narrow bandwidth NetRAD data to generate imagery with high spatial resolution. The high spatial resolution is obtained by applying the principles of tomography to a multi-site radar system which is illuminating a target over a complete angular range of 360 degrees. This paper discusses the current narrowband imaging results using NetRAD and NeXtRAD data.

articleTitle: MIMO radar using frequency incremental waveforms for range-angle localization of targets
abstract: Although multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar has received much attention, MIMO radar misses range information and directional gain in its transmit beampattern and consequently, two-dimensional (range and angle dimensions) localization of targets cannot be directly achieved by the receiver beamforming output peaks. In this paper, we propose the MIMO radar using frequency incremental waveforms, in which the range-angle of targets can be directlyx estimated from the receiver beamforming output peaks. Moreover, a low-complexity multiple signal classification (MUSIC) spectra estimation strategy is proposed. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by numerical results.

articleTitle: Study of RF structure and beam wave interaction system for a W-band sheet beam EIK
abstract: Sheet beam Extended Interaction Klystron (EIK) is an attractive Millimeter Waves (MMW) amplifier because of its high gain per unit length and compact configuration, which can be used in radar transmission system. In this paper, RF structure and beam wave interaction system of W band sheet beam EIK has been designed. A new and effective method of designing and studying the beam wave interaction system is presented in this paper.The whole tube consists of one single-gap cavity, six tri-gaps cavities and one five-gaps cavity. By optimizing the position of cavities, the output power can achieve 30 kW and high gain of 50 dB, which is calculated by three dimensional particle in cell (3D-PIC) software. It provides a powerful basis for the subsequent study of sheet beam EIK.

articleTitle: Tracking dynamics of retrodirective vehicle RADAR with track hold ability
abstract: This paper considers the tracking dynamics of a retrodirective RADAR when applied to a vehicular scenario. The advantages of such a RADAR system are discussed in comparison to a conventional RADAR. More specifically, a “track hold” function is presented for a retrodirective RADAR, which is shown, for typical vehicle turning rates, to be able to maintain the retransmitted beam towards the target during dropouts in the reflected signal. These dropouts could be caused by effects such as variations of target radar cross section with angle of incidence. The “track hold” feature prevents the need for a reacquisition of the target after the dropout and also provides the possibility of using the RADAR to reliably transmit data to the target. The ability to provide a reliable retransmitted beam, even in the absence of a target reflected signal, is a significant improvement compared to traditional mixer based retrodirective antennas, which are unable to maintain the retransmitted signal in the absence of a received signal.

articleTitle: Vessel geometric features extraction in high-resolution SAR images
abstract: Vessel detection and recognition are crucial issues of ocean monitoring utilizing synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. In vessel recognition, refined segmentation is the basis phase of extracting geometric parameters. However, the side lobe and layover effects of vessel target in SAR images affect the segmentation precision. This paper proposes a refined segmentation algorithm of vessel targets in SAR images for vessel geometric parameter extraction. The method extracts the azimuth angle of a vessel firstly, then rotates the target to the vertical direction and realizes the image binarization. The minimum enclosing rectangle (MER) is extracted by using the difference of the number of image pixels and finally the bow and stern of the vessel target is distinguished. Validation results on vessel targets in high resolution SAR images show that the proposed method extracts the MER more accurately and discriminates the bow from the stern effectively.

articleTitle: DOA estimation of low altitude target based on bounded component analysis algorithm
abstract: A recently introduced Blind Source Separation method, called Bounded Component Analysis, is used as preliminary technique to isolate direct path radar wave from ground reflected waves in order to overcome the multipath effect. This method enables the radar to estimate the target angle without any a priori knowledge of the operation environment. The numerical experiments illustrate the potential benefit of the proposed approach relative to classical maximum likelihood method (CMLM) based on free space propagation model.

articleTitle: MIMO radar concept with a towed antenna array
abstract: This paper introduces an alternative type of radar system for airborne surveillance. The system concept comprises a colocated Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar array that is towed by an airborne platform. This could allow the realisation of a wide antenna, giving a narrow beamwidth, that is a usual requirement for localising fixed and moving targets, while optimise the trade-off between the size/weight of a radar array and its length. At the same time, a MIMO structure could allow compensation of errors that may occur due to turbulence during flight. The paper considers methods and proof of concept experimental results which show that the latter is plausible. Correction for antenna deformations is considered as one of the most significant scientific challenges in the concept's further consideration.

articleTitle: A joint optimization for coherent MIMO radar
abstract: This paper deals with the optimization of a set of transmitted sequences and their associated mismatched filters, for the coherent MIMO radar. A minimization problem may be considered, with an objective function that measures for instance the correlations within the set. In the literature, it is usually solved alternatively, meaning that the optimization is performed on the sequences while the mismatched filters are set, and viceversa. In this paper, an iterative method that proceeds jointly is introduced. Sequences are derived with a gradient descent, and mismatched filters are chosen in such a way that they are optimal in the ISL (Integrated Sidelobe Level) sense. Simulations show interesting results, as a joint optimization performs better than a separate one, even with relatively short sequences.

articleTitle: Bayesian radar detection and range estimation of a point-like target
abstract: In this paper, we propose two adaptive decision schemes with enhanced detection and range estimation capabilities for point-like targets buried in Gaussian clutter with unknown spectral properties. To this end, we jointly exploit the spillover of target energy to consecutive range samples and a Bayesian framework where the clutter covariance matrix is modeled as a random matrix obeying the inverse complex Wishart distribution. Under the above assumptions, two Bayesian detectors based on the Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) and the so-called two-step GLRT design procedure are derived. It is shown that the proposed detectors are modified versions of the traditional localization detectors through a colored-loading step utilizing the a priori knowledge and the sample covariance matrix. Finally, performance assessment, conducted on both simulated data and real recorded datasets, demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed detectors compared with their non-Bayesian counterparts.

articleTitle: MIMO versus conventional radar performance against jammers
abstract: It has been claimed that MIMO radars perform better than conventional radars against repeater and hot clutter jammers (jammer signals reflected from the ground into the radar). It is shown here that conventional radars can perform as well if not better than MIMO radars against these jammers as well as against barrage noise jammers. The results are presented in tutorial form without heavy math. Instead physical explanations are given for these results. Applied here to reject the barrage jammer and hot clutter is the Adaptive-Adaptive Array Processing (AAAP) technique which makes use of the information available as to where the jammers are rather than assuming there location is not known as done for the classical sample matrix inversion (SMI) method. This is reminiscent of the Knowledge Aided-STAP (KA-STAP) technique used by DARPA. It also could be called Cognitive Adaptive Array Processing (CAAP). The method reduces the transient time (the number of time samples needed to calculate the interference covariance matrix) by orders of magnitude. Also the interference covariance matrix size is reduced by orders of magnitude and in turn the computation of its matrix inverse. Finally this method reduces the 10's of dB antenna sidelobe degradation usually resulting from using the SMI method. The AAAP technique lends itself well to both the MIMO and conventional array systems when digital beam forming is used which is the future trend.

articleTitle: Preliminary experiments for a new characterization of foliage attenuation in P-band
abstract: Vegetation could degrade the propagation of radar signal, especially the foliage which presents the characteristic to absorb electromagnetic waves. This attenuation depends of the length of the path travelled by the signal through the forest, i.e. the angle of elevation at which the signal propagates. An original concept is proposed to have a magnitude estimation of this absorption for P-band frequencies in function of elevation. The aim is to compare the signal backscattered from air targets received with antennas above and under the canopy. The planes are considered as donor for various elevation angles. One configuration of experimentation is presented in this paper. Unfortunately, it appeared that this first setup was not well adapted to obtain the best results in terms of quantification of the attenuation in function of the angle of elevation. Nevertheless, some first evaluations of foliage attenuation in P-band have been obtained.

articleTitle: Ambiguity function-based ESPRIT-RootMUSIC algorithm for DOD-DOA estimation in MIMO radar
abstract: Considering nonstationary radar signals, a novel ambiguity function-based algorithm is proposed for direction-of-departure (DOD) and direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation in MIMO Radar. By constructing a spatial time-frequency distribution (STFD) matrix, we use the ESPRIT-RootMUSIC method to realize the joint DOD and DOA estimation. The method does not need multiple-dimensional spectrum peak searching and the parameters can be paired automatically. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm. Compared with the method based on pseudo Wigner-Ville distribution, the advantages of extracting the auto term and removing the nosie are more effectively based on ambiguity function. In addition, the accuracy is better than the algorithm based on pseudo Wigner-Ville distribution under the condition of fewer snapshots.

articleTitle: DOA estimation algorithm based on compressed sensing in HF sky-surface wave radar
abstract: High frequency sky-surface wave radar (HFSSWR) utilizes sky-wave transmission and surface-wave receiving to implement further range detection, which proposes the higher requirements for angle estimation precision with few array elements and single snapshot. According to the spatial sparseness of receiving targets, compressed sensing (CS) could high probability recover absent channel signals and obtain accurate target azimuth information. Commonly, continuous parameter region need to be divided into finite discrete grid points for building redundancy dictionary base. However, the grid density is limited by the computational complexity and restricted isometry property, so the direction of arrival (DOA) of the targets usually may be not on the initialized sampling grid in practical situations, which would lead to angle estimation mismatch. In this paper, a novel polar interpolation direction estimation (PIDE) algorithm based on CS was proposed to obtain higher precision with single snapshot and sparse receiving array. The results of numerical experiment based on the measured and simulative data demonstrate the advantage of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Interference mitigation for airborne MIMO radar
abstract: Coherent multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar has been shown to offer many advantages over conventional phased-array radars. However, it is know that the overall transmit gain of coherent MIMO radar is lower than that of phased-array radar due to the employment of orthogonal waveforms, which leads to lower signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels. Although subarray-based MIMO radar (e.g. phased-MIMO radar) provides higher transmit gain compared to coherent MIMO radar, the transmit degrees of freedoms (DOFs) are reduced as a trade-off. In this work, the loss of SNR in coherent MIMO radar is compensated by using longer coherent processing intervals (CPI) in combination with a reduced dimension interference mitigation algorithm. It is demonstrated by simulation results that once the SNR loss is compensated for, coherent MIMO radar outperforms both phased-array radars and subarray-based MIMO radar, in airborne radar ground moving target detection.

articleTitle: A high-accuracy interferometrie SAR images registration strategy combined with cross correlation and spectral diversity
abstract: For the image registration of interferometric SAR, there is a contradiction between the registration accuracy and the robustness based on the traditional cross correlation and spectral diversity methods. To eliminate the contradiction, this paper proposes an image registration strategy combined with the respective advantages of above two methods. Its improvements are summarized as follows. Firstly, it divides the image registration process into two main steps. Step one is oriented to the image registration in the range direction based on cross correlation to enhance the robustness. Step two is oriented to the image registration in the azimuth direction based on spectral diversity to ensure the registration accuracy. Secondly, a method for detecting and correcting the singular values in the range pixels offsets is proposed in step one. It can reduce the impact of low-correlation regions. Finally, a hybrid filtering method is introduced for the azimuth pixels offsets in step two to reduce the impact of phase noise. Airborne dual-antenna data are employed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Target detection in bistatic radar sea clutter using stationary wavelet transforms
abstract: Radar backscatter from the sea-surface is typically nonstationary and may contain sea-spikes which resemble targets and can cause false detections in a radar system. To improve detection performance, this paper investigates a technique based on stationary wavelet transforms (SWT) and demonstrates its performance on both monostatic and bistatic seaclutter data. By exploiting the different components (subbands) of the SWT decomposition, this technique can better distinguish between the different spectral components of the returned signal. The detection performance is measured by Monte Carlo simulation with a cell averaging constant false alarm rate (CA-CFAR) detector. The most appropriate choice of sub-band is selected using an a entropy based metric.

articleTitle: Bright sapphire - LF SAR imagery - A first look
abstract: A potential solution to remote sensing through building and facilities walls from outside of the structure is to use Low-Frequency RF sensing and Synthetic Aperture Radar techniques. This provides the advantage of remote observation and greater coverage than existing through-wall observation techniques than require close proximity to the wall. The Bright Sapphire II instrument is a low frequency wideband quad polar SAR and offers such measurement capability. The first results of airborne trials are presented.

articleTitle: Target detection within sea clutter based on multi-scale cumulative high-order characteristics
abstract: As a high-order scale characteristic, the lacunarity can characterize the speed of the irregular fluctuation of the sea clutter sequence, and show different trends when the target exists. Using this difference property, it is proposed to use the multi-scale cumulative lacunarity characteristic to form detection statistics, which is used to distinguish between sea clutter and target echoes. Verified by the X-band real sea clutter data, the results show that under low signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) conditions, compared with simple fractal dimension, the multi-scale cumulative lacunarity characteristic can significantly enhance the difference between sea clutter and target echo, and improve the detection performance of weak target in sea clutter background.

articleTitle: An electromagnetic modelling environment for the design of radomes for AESA radar
abstract: The lack of a one-size fits all solution to the electromagnetic modelling of radomes for AESA applications (full-wave solvers are not a panacea) has necessitated the development of a modelling environment in which different methods (geometrical optics, physical optics and MoM) can be easily combined. The philosophy behind the modelling environment is described, and an example C-sandwich radome, optimised for an AESA antenna, is presented, together with a novel hybrid approach to flashlobe prediction and assessment.

articleTitle: A composite joint sub-aperture imaging along nonlinear trajectories
abstract: In this paper, an imaging algorithm for the airborne radar system maneuvering along an arbitrary trajectory is proposed. The algorithm aims at wide-angle imaging with incomplete measurements from the nonlinear trajectory. The proposed composite joint sub-aperture imaging algorithm provides high reconstruction quality and supports efficient data collection policy. The image can be reconstructed by combining image patches corresponding to non-overlapping sub-apertures. The image patch is obtained by compressive sensing with joint sparse representation of the scene. Numerical results have proved that the proposed algorithm is highly effective and capable of image reconstruction without much loss in quality, especially on objects signature and contour.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of polarimetric signatures for propeller modulation
abstract: Radar detection of aerial targets plays a major role in security, defense, and surveillance applications. The propeller modulation generated by rotating blades provides a useful way for the flying targets detection, but it requires a deep understanding of the electromagnetic scattering process. To reveal the backscattering characteristics of the propeller, the scattering matrix is derived in time-frequency domain. Polarimetric signatures of the rotating blades are analyzed by target decomposition. Further simulations for the rotor indicate that the multi-polarization measurements can provide more information about the rotating blades.

articleTitle: Joint high resolution imaging and autofocusing technique via an iterative method for multistatic passive radar
abstract: The performance of the multistatic passive radar imaging system (MPRIS) based on illuminators of opportunity is not as good as traditional SAR/ISAR due to the narrow bandwidth of the radiated signal and the unevenly distribution of the non-cooperation illuminators. Moreover, the inaccurate position measurement of illuminators, receivers and the target would cause phase errors in the target echo and the quality of the image would further subject to degradation. With the motivation to improve the performance of the MPRIS, an imaging algorithm based on the principle of tomographic imaging is presented. On account of the sparse distribution of the scatterer of the target, the compressed sensing algorithm is extended to the multistatic configuration to realize the super resolution image formation. In addition, an autofocusing technique based on the multistatic observation model is proposed. By defining a quality measure of the image, the phase error is found by iteratively solving an equation which is derived by optimizing the quality measure of the image. The convergence and performance of the presented autofocusing technique have been validated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Structural antennas for 3cm radar onboard multi-rotor UAV
abstract: A series of 3cm amateur band radar antennas suitable for installation on a cinematic grade multi-rotor UAV were considered. A wideband open waveguide mouth antenna was developed that can be made from the existing arms of a multirotor UAV without any increase in weight for side-looking wall detection ranging radar. For downward looking radio altimeter, cutting slots in the arms to form slotted waveguide antennas was shown in simulation to be possible both in terms of covering the entire 3cm band from 10 to 10.5 GHz and without overly weakening the arms as structural members.

articleTitle: Fast time domain algorithm for missile-borne bistatic forward-looking SAR based on ground elliptical polar coordinate
abstract: Missile-borne bistatic forward-looking synthetic aperture radar (BFSAR) plays a significant role in precise terminal guidance and attacking of the missile. However, its special configuration and operational mode would induce the large spatial variances and serious range-azimuth coupling of echo data, which increases the difficulty of the precise image formation. In this paper, a fast time domain algorithm based on the ground elliptical polar coordinate is proposed to focus the missile-borne BFSAR data precisely. It represents the subimages on the ground elliptical polar grids to reduce the computational burden. The imaging geometry and signal model of the missile-borne BFSAR are firstly established. Then, the implementation of processing the missile-borne BFSAR data using the fast time domain algorithm is presented. Finally, simulation experiment is carried out to prove the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Classification of CommSense data using learning algorithms
abstract: In our previous work we have shown the design of a Communication based Sensing (CommSense) system. The current work presents analysis of the data captured by a CommSense system. Analysis is performed using Support Vector Machines (SVM) and a Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) which are commonly used supervised learning algorithms. The predicted results are presented in the form of a confusion matrix and an analysis is presented showing the percentage of error in prediction.

articleTitle: Optical link design for a maritime radar system
abstract: The mast weight is a critical design specification of any maritime vessel and therefore the design of radar must make sure the weight of the system is distributed appropriately. The use of RF on fibre technology gives the radar system designer the ability to shift (and reduce) the weight of the system in a way that is not possible if using standard RF distribution methods. In an RF on fibre link the RF signal is intensity modulated onto an optical carrier and distributed from the mast head to below deck through a multichannel optical rotating joint. The most critical requirements of the optical distribution system are to reduce mast mass, provide high dynamic range, minimise increase in Noise Figure (NF) and exhibit low phase noise even in the presence of vibration. This paper describes the design, build and testing process of a ruggedized transmitter and receiver modules that include an optical rotating joint (ORJ). The final section of this paper presents a summary of the performance and future development recommendations.

articleTitle: Piecewise cumulative Weibull modelling of radar cross section
abstract: Statistical models of radar cross section in radar system simulation are common for providing data to test the interaction of the target tracking systems and the decision making activities. For many decades, the scintillation of the target RCS has been represented using models developed by Swerling. This paper investigates how well the Swerling models relate to the RCS of modern targets, and outlines a computationally simple approach to generating representative random RCS values based on a piecewise approximation of the target RCS cumulative distribution function that employs two sections of a Weibull distribution, and also provides simple mechanisms to mimic the temporal correlation effects of scintillation seen with target manoeuvre and the variation of RCS with range.

articleTitle: Coherent radar sea clutter modeling and simulation
abstract: A two component clutter model is proposed to aid in the simulation of the spatio-temporal characteristics of radar sea clutter backscatter returns collected from moving airborne platforms. The simulation approach is seen to reproduce key characteristic of the real data and supports the development of both new detection approaches and effective test and verification programs for radar procurements.

articleTitle: A comparison of GMTI detectors for dual-channel ScanSAR
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the performance of three ground moving target indication (GMTI) detectors for a dual-channel SAR system operating in the stripmap SAR and ScanSAR acquisition modes. Displaced Phase Center Antenna (DPCA), Extended DPCA (EDPCA) and Imaging STAP (ISTAP) detectors are tested and compared. The impact of a bursted data acquisition on the signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio (SCNR) is analyzed, specifically with regard to the across-track speed of the target and its along-track position. Results indicate that ISTAP has the overall best performance for dual-channel stripmap SAR and ScanSAR. Scalloping due to bursted data acquisition is also shown to affect SCNR values for all three detectors.

articleTitle: A motion error compensation method for linear array three-dimensional synthetic aperture radar
abstract: In the last decade, an increased interest has been devoted to linear array 3-D synthetic aperture radar(LA-3D-SAR) in radar field. Compared with the traditional 2-D SAR, the motion error of LA-3D-SAR is more various and can result in serious defocusing phenomenon. It is difficult to compensate these errors respectively. For this problem, a 3-D autofocus backprojection(BP) algorithm based on phase error estimation is proposed. The motion error can be modeled as the phase error in range compression domain. Therefore, the method uses the estimated phase value obtained by the coordinate descent method to compensate various motion errors. The sharpness value of 3-D image is treated as the objective function of the coordinate descent method. The simulation results show that the proposed method can obtain the wellfocused 3-D image and the focusing effect is close to the error-free imaging result basically. And processing of experimental data demonstrates the efficacy of this method.

articleTitle: Complex envelope estimation of direct-path pulse signal based on real data
abstract: The problems of the influence of noise and multi-path interference and reconstruction of direct-path reference signals are researched in this paper. In order to estimate the complex envelope of the direct-path reference signals, the techniques of blind equalization are researched. An improved CMA+MMA algorithm is proposed, and the validity of the algorithm is proved by using the experimental real data.

articleTitle: The next generation of spaceborne radars for cloud and precipitation measurements
abstract: NASA's Earth Science Technology Office (ESTO) is currently developing advanced instrument concepts and technologies for the next generation of spaceborne atmospheric radars for clouds and precipitation measurements. Two representative examples are the Radar in a CubeSat (RainCube) - a miniaturized Ka-band precipitation intensity profiling radar for operation on a 6U CubeSat bus; and the Multi-Application Smallsat Tri-band Radar (MASTR) - a Ku/Ka/W band, electronic scanning, and Doppler atmospheric radar. These radar concepts will be capable of providing information on both the state and the process of the atmospheric water (as opposed to just the state information provided by existing spaceborne radars) to fill the current observational gaps in the advancement of weather and climate models.

articleTitle: Aperiodic linear array pattern optimization based on vector mapping and harmony search algorithm
abstract: To come up with the problem of designing aperiodic linear arrays with multiple constraints, a pattern synthesis technique based on vector mapping and Improved Harmony Search (IHS) Algorithm is proposed to reduce the peak side-lobe level (PSLL) of the array. The constraints include the number of elements, the array aperture, and the minimum and the maximum distance between neighboring elements. On the condition that the feasible solution space remains unchangeable, a special vector mapping is applied between the element spacings and the initial variables. Thus, the constrained optimization problem is simply transformed to a non-constrained problem with greater degree of freedom (DoF). Design case found in the literature is simulated to compare the performance of these algorithms. Simulation results reveal the high efficiency, robustness and low computation cost of the proposed method.

articleTitle: CubeSAT based bistatic passive radar for ballistic missile defence: Feasibility study
abstract: The demand for Ballistic Missile Defence (BMD) systems able to provide early warning and classification has grown in the last decades as consequence of production of missiles always more technological and efficient. In this paper the feasibility study of new low budget space-borne radar for supporting BMD is presented. The idea is to take advantages jointly by the use of Passive Bistitic Radar (PBR) and Forward Scattering (FS) configuration to guarantee high capabilities for target detection and identification.

articleTitle: A hybrid algorithm for sparse circular array SLL suppression under the constraint of ADRR
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid algorithm to suppress the sidelobe level (SLL) of the non-uniform sparse circular array. It takes full advantages of each single algorithm to obtain a low peak side-lobe level (PSLL), in which Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is used as the global searcher to optimize the positions of array elements and Second-order Cone Programming (SOCP) is used as the local searcher to obtain the optimal weight excitation. We also propose an effective method to optimize the amplitude dynamic range ratio (ADRR), making the system achievable in practical application. Results indicate that our algorithm is competitive and easy to realize.

articleTitle: Coherent sea clutter modelling
abstract: This paper describes a clutter model that simulates spatially and temporally correlated coherent radar returns from the sea. Range-Doppler maps are generated to compare a homogeneous clutter model with this sea clutter model to illustrate the advantages that coherent processing could provide with respect to detecting small targets in a maritime environment.

articleTitle: Designing practical spectrally constrained waveforms for HFSWR by successive convex approximations and projections
abstract: In this paper, we consider the design of practical transmit waveforms for a high frequency surface wave radar system operating in a congested spectral environment where the radar must adhere to strict regulations on the interference it can cause to on-going communications. The ideal waveform would be constant amplitude, and have low autocorrelation sidelobes, all while meeting the imposed spectral constraints; however, it is impossible to know a priori that such a waveform exists. We propose an algorithm based on alternating successive convex approximations and projections to design waveforms which meet strict spectral constraints and autocorrelation sidelobe constraints while minimizing amplitude modulation. In simulation, the proposed algorithm is found to converge rapidly and the resulting waveforms have better pulse compression properties than other similar methods from the relevant literature.

articleTitle: Landmine discrimination using spectral features from Ground Penetrating Radar data
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for Landmine discrimination from Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) data using spectral features extracted from identified region of interest and Support Vector Machine (SVM) as classifier. In our approach, images obtained from GPR vehicle mounted system are first pre-processed using moving average subtraction filter and median filter to suppress background and noise. Least Mean Square algorithm applied on three dimensions (3D-LMS) of GPR data is used as anomaly detector to identify region of interest. Spectral features are extracted from the region of interest using Fourier transform. Feature vector is formed from salient points of Fourier transform, which are given to support vector machine during training and testing phases of classification. Classifier was trained using samples collected for different soil conditions, different targets, and clutter at various burial depths. Performance of our proposed method is measured in terms of classification accuracy and our proposed method using spectral features has shown a better performance compared to using edge features for landmine discrimination.

articleTitle: A computationally efficient detector: Using both the test and training data for disturbance correlation estimation
abstract: This paper examines a target detection problem in colored Gaussian disturbance with an unknown covariance matrix. In many classic adaptive detectors, the covariance estimator is formed by using only the training data. This necessitates calculating a new covariance estimator for each cell under test (CUT) during the cell-by-cell target search process. We consider herein an alternative approach that forms the covariance matrix estimate by using both test and training data for detection in homogeneous environments. This approach is computationally much more efficient since the covariance matrix estimator is computed only once and can be applied for target detection at each CUT. Using this estimator, we propose a new detector with two tunable parameters, which includes several existing detectors as special cases. Closed-form expressions for the probabilities of false alarm and detection are derived in the matched and mismatched cases. Simulation results reveal that the rejection capability of mismatched signals of the proposed detector can be flexibly controlled by adjusting its tunable parameters.

articleTitle: Antenna beam broadening optimization in space-borne SAR with AESA
abstract: In this paper, a beam broadening problem solution for SAR applications with two-dimensional active electrically scanning array (AESA) is presented. An aperture field distribution optimization problem considering observation geometry and reflection properties of the ground is formulated. A shaped pattern synthesis problem is divided in two separate problems: beam broadening in elevation and azimuth planes. In elevation plane, the problem is solved using orthogonal aperture polynomials approach and a global optimization algorithm. An active electrically scanning array with DBF in azimuth plane is considered for beam broadening. Solution for azimuth plane beam broadening, featuring small number of elements and large element spacing, is also presented.

articleTitle: Joint multi-target DOD and DOA estimation in bistatic MIMO radar exploiting 2-level nested arrays
abstract: In this paper, we investigate joint estimation of direction-of-departure (DOD) and direction-of-arrival (DOA) of multiple targets in bistatic MIMO radar exploiting nested arrays. By configuring 2-level nested arrays in the transmit and receive arrays, a large number of virtual array apertures are introduced. Therefore, the spatial resolution of the MIMO radar system is significantly enhanced. Moreover, the maximum number of the identifiable targets is enlarged to a higher degree compared with traditional uniform linear arrays. The signal model is formulated by the exploitation of the nested arrays. A novel row extraction method is proposed to construct an observed data vector for joint angle estimation. The simulation results validate the theoretical algorithm.

articleTitle: High-order interacting multiple model filter based on mixture transition distribution
abstract: A novel nth-order interacting multiple model (IMMn) filter based on the mixture transition distribution (MTD) for maneuvering target tracking referred as IMMn-MTD filter is proposed here. It adopts MTD model rather than fully parameterized high-order Markov chain (MC) to approximate the model sequence transition probabilities. Since only a few independent parameters need to be fixed in MTD model, IMMn-MTD is more flexible compared with the high-order MC mothed. This approach simultaneously possesses the advantage in accuracy because high order model sequence is evaluated. Simulations are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Suppressing the effects of ionospheric scintillation on geosynchronous SAR by optimised orbit design
abstract: An L band geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR) will be sensitive to ionosphere scintillation because of its low carrier frequency. Meanwhile, because of the high orbit, GEO SAR has a higher probability to meet ionospheric scintillation. In this paper, we propose an orbit strategy for eliminating the impacts of ionospheric scintillation. It is realized by selecting a proper orbit element (time past perigee) to avoid imaging for the sensitive region of ionospheric scintillation during the eruption time interval of ionospheric scintillation with the highest probability. Finally, the simulation based on systems tool kit (STK) software was conducted to verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Lunar-based synthetic aperture radar: Preliminary system design and performance analysis
abstract: Lunar-based SAR, as a relatively new concept, have some potential in spatial continuity observation and other characters. Different from current spaceborne SAR systems, the lunar orbit is much higher. A relatively low resolution for earth area observation could be a applied observation mode of lunar-based SAR which can avoid the north-south ambiguity when lunar-based SAR treated as a kind of planet radar. This paper studies the Doppler characteristics of the lunar-based SAR using numerical simulation. Then a preliminary design of lunar-based SAR id given to show its potential and some limitations. Simulation indicates that lunar-based SAR is qualified in wide swath Earth observation but have some limitations for system implementation currently.

articleTitle: Knowledge based space Doppler adaptive processing for imaging of moving targets in strong ground clutter
abstract: A priori knowledge can be exploited to increase clutter cancellation performance. This, in particular, applies in the case of Multichannel high resolution SAR systems in scenarios where also non-cooperative moving targets are present. Space Doppler Adaptive Processing has been proven as a viable solution in this case although it needs a large number of i.i.d training data. Prior knowledge can be used to relax this demanding condition. Two approaches (ITFS and Bayesian) are described and results on simulated data are shown.

articleTitle: A fast and accurate estimator of the plane of reflection using MIMO radar
abstract: Consider a MIMO radar which is placed near a plane reflector. Given a set of time-of-flight measurements between each transmitter-receiver pair, we are interested in accurately estimating the distance to the plane and its orientation relative to the radar. The problem is inspired by an application investigated at Teledyne Defence Australia in low-visibility landing radar [1]. In previous work [2], it was demonstrated that very accurate results could be obtained by extensions of the common tangent algorithm [3] to account for multiple transmitters. However, the algorithms so obtained were iterative optimisers. In this paper, we seek a non-iterative estimator that is simple to implement and fast to compute which nevertheless maintains good accuracy. We show that the squared-distance matrix arising from the time-of-flight measurements, through novel processing, can yield accurate distance and orientation estimates from its eigendecomposition. We demonstrate through numerical simulation that, while not attaining the Cramér-Rao Lower Bound as the iterative optimisers do, accuracy is still very high.

articleTitle: Multi-polarization radar imaging using two-level block matching pursuit
abstract: In this paper, we propose a two-level block matching pursuit (TLBMP) algorithm based on a probabilistic graph model for multi-polarization radar imaging. In high-resolution radar images, most indoor targets occupy some clustered pixels instead of only an isolated pixel. In addition, multi-polarization sensing is used to obtain more independent observations under the joint sparsity framework. TLBMP exploits both the clustering property and the joint sparsity pattern of the multi-polarization radar images. Experiments based on real radar data show that, compared to some popular algorithms, TLBMP provides more informative image with higher target-to-clutter-ratio (TCR).
